Execution order (unquote, then guard, then queue) and response bodies and status codes are preserved line for line.

Naming is consistent: the new helper uses a single underscore, like the existing helpers `_check_path_safe` and `_process_bulk_commands`. The route handlers keep their name-mangled `__handle_*` names, so the route wiring in add_routes (lines 66-70) and any tests that call `_ControllerHandler__handle_action_*` still resolve. Pending: I did not open test_controller_handler.py to confirm how the tests call the handlers.

The `Controller.Command(action, file_name)` + `WebResponseActionCallback` + `queue_command` sequence now appears twice: in `_dispatch_command` (lines 97-100) and in `_process_bulk_commands` (lines 349-352). That is below the rule of three, and the bulk path deliberately queues everything before waiting, so a shared abstraction is not warranted. No finding.

Minor inconsistency: `_dispatch_command` annotates `action` as the string "Controller.Command.Action", while `_process_bulk_commands` (line 299) uses the unquoted `Controller.Command.Action`. `Controller` is already imported at module level, so the quotes are unnecessary. This is cosmetic, not a finding.

No new imports, dependencies, cycles or cross-module coupling. The change is confined to ControllerHandler internals, and its only importer, web_app_builder.py, uses only the public constructor and add_routes, so it is unaffected.

findings.problem: The new `_dispatch_command` decides whether to run the path-traversal guard from a caller-supplied `guard: bool`. Three call sites (lines 125, 134, 143) each set `guard=True` by hand. The class already defines `_GUARDED_ACTIONS` (lines 159-163), which lists exactly the same three actions (EXTRACT, DELETE_LOCAL, DELETE_REMOTE), and the bulk path already uses it (`if action in self._GUARDED_ACTIONS`, line 337). The single-action path and the bulk path now have two separate sources of truth for which actions are guarded. The gate is only partly met: `_GUARDED_ACTIONS` has one existing use, not the two needed to call it an established pattern, so this stays low.
findings.title: Guard policy for single-action dispatch is a per-call boolean, duplicating the existing _GUARDED_ACTIONS source of truth
findings.why_it_matters: If someone adds a new destructive action to `_GUARDED_ACTIONS`, the bulk endpoint gets the traversal check but a new single-action endpoint skips it unless the author also remembers `guard=True`. The safe behavior should be the default, not something each caller has to opt into. The refactor already created a shared helper, so this was the natural point to merge the two policies.

agent_notes: Scope: one file. The five single-action handlers (__handle_action_queue/stop/extract/delete_local/delete_remote) in src/python/web/handler/controller.py now share one helper, _dispatch_command (lines 76-105). Routes in add_routes (lines 66-70) still bind to the same mangled handler names, so the HTTP routes, verbs and URL shapes are unchanged.

Behavior matches the old code. For each endpoint I compared old against new: unquote first, then the path guard (only for EXTRACT, DELETE_LOCAL and DELETE_REMOTE), then Command, callback and queue_command, then wait with _ACTION_TIMEOUT=30.0, then 504 'Operation timed out', success 200 or callback.error with callback.error_code. All of this is preserved, and so are the five success-message templates, byte for byte.

Path-traversal control is kept, not loosened. Every handler that guarded before passes guard=True (lines 125, 134, 143), and the guard still runs after unquote (lines 92-96), so double-encoded '../' is still decoded before the realpath containment check in _check_path_safe (lines 172-188). QUEUE and STOP were never guarded in the old single-action code, and the bulk path (_GUARDED_ACTIONS, lines 159-163) doesn't guard them either. That is unchanged and consistent.

Format-string safety is unchanged. success_msg is always a constant literal from the call site, and file_name goes in as a format() argument, not as the template. A file name containing '{' or '}' therefore cannot break or inject into the format, exactly as before.

Name mangling still works. Inside _dispatch_command, self.__controller is written in the ControllerHandler class body, so it mangles to _ControllerHandler__controller as before. The new helper has a single underscore and is reachable from subclasses and tests. That adds internal surface but changes no existing contract.

Public API and importers: web_app_builder.py only constructs ControllerHandler(controller, local_path) and calls add_routes, and neither changed. The unit tests at src/python/tests/unittests/test_web/test_handler/test_controller_handler.py call _ControllerHandler__handle_action_queue/delete_local/delete_remote/extract directly (lines 45, 134, 795-841). Those names still exist, so the tests stay compatible. src/python/docs/name-mangling-tradeoff.md also still lists these method names correctly.
Schema and migrations: none. Performance: none. Removing one local variable and an else branch has no measurable effect, and the 30s per-request blocking wait is the same as before.

Blast radius if the helper had a bug: all five single-action endpoints (queue, stop, extract, delete_local, delete_remote) would fail together, where before a bug could hit only one. That is the usual tradeoff of deduplicating code. The bulk endpoint (_process_bulk_commands) is separate and not affected.
Verdict: a pure refactor with no breaking API, schema or performance changes, and the path-safety control is preserved. Shippable as-is.
